why_not_fixed_in_this_tick: The two legs disagree with each other about the space the syscall copies into: basic_copy reads the result back with LD/PRT (RAM), multi_byte asserts five values with cpu._mem_read(image, ...) (pixels). No measurement can settle which the ABI intends, so the choice is a design question, not a test edit.
options_cheapest_first: (1) Re-author the test's fixture setup/readback to pixel space with cpu._mem_write(image, addr, val) — the same API multi_byte already reads back with; keeps the syscall ABI as the spec; ~10 line edits; gate = 9/9 legs green + non-vacuity (disable the 0x11 branch -> the copy legs must go RED).
(2) Rule that 0x11 copies RAM words (self.memory) instead: basic_copy's LD/PRT then works, but multi_byte's five image-space assertions must be re-authored; the engine changes instead of the test.
(3) Alias the test's addresses between RAM and image at bake time so both APIs agree — most invasive, touches the memory model.
(4) Re-author the whole file against the measured image geometry (fixtures placed outside the program's pixel span) — largest, but removes the whole class.
